seoTitle: Free Line Numbering Tool: Add Line Numbers to Text
metaDescription: Prefix each line of text with a number, choosing the start value, separator and alignment, and optionally skipping empty lines. Free, in-browser.
intro: Add line numbers to pasted text. Choose the starting number, the separator, whether to right-align the numbers and whether to skip empty lines.
why:
Numbered lines are useful when you quote code in a review, refer to a clause in a contract, share a log excerpt in a ticket or prepare a script. Most plain text editors do not show numbers you can copy, so the numbers are lost when you paste.

This tool puts a number at the start of every line of the text you paste. You can start from any number, set the separator, such as a colon and a space, or a tab, and right-align the numbers so the text lines up when the count passes 9 or 99. If you skip empty lines, they are left blank and not numbered, and the numbering continues on the next line with text. Everything is done in your browser.
howTo: Paste your text into the input box.
Set the starting number and the separator, for example a colon and a space.
Choose right-aligned numbers and whether to skip empty lines.
Run the tool and copy the numbered text.

faq.q: Can I start numbering from a number other than 1?
faq.a: Yes. Set the start value in the options, for example 100 to continue from an earlier section. Zero and negative start values also work.

faq.q: What does skip empty lines do?
faq.a: Empty lines are left unnumbered and do not use up a number, so the numbers continue in sequence on the lines that have text.

faq.q: How do I remove line numbers later?
faq.a: Use the find and replace tool with a regex such as ^\s*\d+: to strip them, adjusting the separator to match what you used.
